In March of this year, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed there are no plans for future Mac Pro hardware.

A new report from Bloomberg today sheds further light on the ins and outs of Apple's Mac Pro strategy and reveals a surprising detail about a project Apple once developed...

Inside Apple's abandoned Mac Pro plans

In his latest Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman explains that "abandoning the Mac Pro" was "not always the plan" inside Apple. Gurman reiterates a previously reported view: Apple's original idea was to follow up the "Ultra" chip with another chip called "Extreme."

The report states: "To my knowledge, Apple once developed the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme chips, but ultimately scrapped these projects due to cost and demand considerations."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware that was being developed, Gurman says Apple had two models (codenamed J170 and J190) in development internally, but they were never brought to market.

Perhaps the most intriguing detail in the report is that one of them actually featured an Intel processor:

Apple ultimately discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its website, and steered buyers toward the Mac Studio. Although this ending was long foreshadowed, for enthusiasts of Mac Pro hardware it still marks the quiet end of an era.

What are your thoughts on Apple's decision to shut down the Mac Pro product line rather than continue pushing the "Extreme" chip into the Apple Silicon era? Let us know in the comments.
